label: QSFP56 200GBASE-FR4 2 km
notes: The short end of the 200G rung and the pair to qsfp56-200g-er4-40km: 200GBASE-FR4 is a 2 km class, so a 200G service inside one campus, or between two halls of a DC, wants this row rather than the 40 km one, whose 10 dB class floor would put a pad on a 300 m run. Figures: Gigalight GQS-SPO201-FR4CZB data sheet (200GBASE-FR4, QSFP56, uncooled DFB, IEEE 802.3bs FR4), optical characteristics table, per lane - average launch power -4.2..+4.7 dBm, average receive power -8.2..+4.7 dBm, receive power (OMAouter) maximum +4.5 dBm, receiver sensitivity (OMAouter) -6.0 dBm, stressed receiver sensitivity (OMAouter) -3.6 dBm, damage threshold +5.7 dBm, four CWDM lanes 1264.5-1271 / 1284.5-1291 / 1304.5-1311 / 1324.5-1331 nm. Corroborated by the Hypertec QSFP56-200GB-4FR4-AO sheet, which prints the same -4.2/+4.7 launch and -8.2/+4.7 receive per lane and the same 10.7 dBm total. The row keeps the average receive power minimum (-8.2), not the OMAouter sensitivity (-6.0): a launch figure is subtracted from an average receive figure, and the 2.2 dB between them is OMA-to-average conversion on this lane count, not slack. Budget -4.2 - (-8.2) = 4.0 dB, the FR4 class channel insertion loss, and receive maximum equals launch maximum (+4.7), so the class floor is 0 dB and this optic never needs a pad - a back-to-back patch reads 3.40 dB of headroom and lands marginal on the margin band, not on overload (measured). The consequence a buyer has to see before quoting: 4.0 dB is a short budget and the default 3 dB design margin eats most of it. 2 km of G.652.D at 0.35 dB/km is 0.70 dB, two SC/APC matings 0.60 dB, so the declared 2 km link is 1.30 dB of ODN and 2.70 dB of headroom - inside the class by 2.70 dB but BELOW the 3 dB margin, a fail; the last length that clears the margin is 1.158 km (3.00 dB), 1 km reads 3.05 dB and marginal, and 5 km reads 1.65 dB, 10 km -0.10 dB, both fail (all measured). Inside a building with one patch that is fine and expected; between buildings it is the reason the ER4 row exists. The sheet's 'extended link length of 10 km' note is deliberately NOT taken: that is an FEC-enabled claim at this module's discretion rather than the class, and reach and loss are separate verdicts anyway. The row reads the same shape as qsfp-dd-400g-fr4-2km (2 km: 2.80 dB of headroom, fail; back-to-back 3.50 dB, marginal), so this is what a 4 dB class optic does under a 3 dB margin, not a fault in the row. Four CWDM lanes on one duplex pair - 1310 nm because the engine budgets one wavelength, worst-lane figures, and the cable's 0.35 dB/km window applies. Class figures for one module family, not a purchase-tested part - replace the row with the optic actually bought before pricing a build.
